Command: Do not build an altar of hewn stones
Summary: The command: Do not build an altar of hewn stones (Exodus 20:25). An altar of earth or unhewn stone kept human tool-work off the place of sacrifice.
Commandment: Do not build an altar of hewn stones.
Application: It cannot be practised as written without the standing temple and Aaronic priesthood; its enduring lesson is God's holiness, the cost of atonement, and worship offered exactly as God appoints.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: lifting a tool upon the altar pollutes it (Exodus 20:25).
Function: An altar of earth or unhewn stone kept human tool-work off the place of sacrifice — a ceremonial law of the plain altar. Its goal was to keep the altar unpolluted: lifting a tool upon it polluted it. The evil was human craft imposed on God's altar, the builder's tool-work claiming a share in the holy place. It restrained that by the unhewn stone: the altar was made of what God made, not of what man's tool had shaped.
